checks: The minimal face is generated by P intersect F_p. Orthogonal projection of a full parameter leaves every face denominator unchanged. Along the exposing ray all off-face denominators eventually become positive and diverge, and their contributions tend to zero for every N>0. In a proper face some off-face atom has positive mass, precluding full attainment; in the full face both parameter spaces and sums coincide.

For positive face dimension the closed relative ball bounds the parameter domain by r times its norm less than 1. Every boundary point of this finite intersection of open affine constraints has a zero denominator and no negative ones. Since its associated positive-mass term diverges, the sublevel at alpha=0 is a nonempty compact subset of the domain. The Hessian has positive coefficient N(N+1) and the offsets span V_p, giving strict convexity on the convex domain. In dimension zero the only parameter is zero and the only atom on the face is p.

At the interior optimum the derivative vanishes in V_p and the escort mean deviation lies in V_p, so the deviation itself is zero. Pairing it with alpha_p proves that the sum of the escorts equals the sum weighted by their denominators, which is exactly E_p. Each escort is positive on P_p, and all vanish off it by definition.

The exposing functional forces every feasible barycentric row to be supported on P_p. Its weighted denominator sum equals 1. The Hölder exponents N+1 and (N+1)/N are conjugate and exceed 1 for every real N>0. At the escort row the two sequences of powered summands are proportional, giving equality. Strict concavity of the positive weighted sum of the coordinate powers 0<s<1 on the entire simplex, including zero coordinates, gives a unique maximizer.

Mixing optimal rows proves concavity of the root of the value across all of Q, including across faces. The normalization factors out M to power 1/(N+1); the coefficient (s-1)^(-1)=-(N+1) reverses maximization, yielding precisely the displayed negative minimum Rényi formula. Its logarithm has positive argument because some lambda_z is positive and every pi_z is positive.

For the fiber statement, the centroid of each full-dimensional positive-volume compact convex fiber lies in its interior (a supporting hyperplane through it would contradict the strictly positive integral of the inward distance). A ball scaled by any one strictly positive row entry, with the other entries fixed at their centroids, gives the required ball in the assumed Minkowski inclusion.
